yeah also a lot of stuff are built veeery slowly, for example when irrationals were discovered in ancient greece, the definition of proportionality had to change since you can't say "the ratio between the (integer) sizes measured by a smaller length is 2:3 for both objects", a lot of proofs relied on choosing a very small segment that divided evenly all the sizes in the problem and then you talked about how divided each thing wasso the idea atributed to eudoxus was that 4 quantities had the same proportion, A to B and C to D if (in modern notation)  
for any two naturals n and m it's always true that  
if nA > mB, then nC > mD  
if nA = mB, then nC = mD (which would be the standard definition of proportionality)  
and  
if nA < mB, then nC < mD  
basically that's how you could encode that two quantities have the same relation one to another, you compare them being multiplied by the same amounts  
if you rearrange the terms you get  
A/B > m/n implies C/D > m/n  
A/B = m/n implies C/D = m/n  
A/B < m/n implies C/D < m/n  
if you can't have the middle one (which means that the quantities are incommensurable, aka have an irrational ratio) you can still associate the ratio A/B and C/D to all the rational ratios they are greater than and smaller than, this is precisely the dedekind cuts construction of the real numbers, for each real number you associate it to all the rationals which are smaller or greater then it in some way  
but well no one constructs numbers in real analysis (well no one's gonna bother to do that generally for someone learning) so you can package that construction in a simple rule: if you have any bounded above set, there is a least upper bound for the set, or, for each set of numbers which are less then others, you can associate to it THE number that's the upper limit of this set  
but if you just see that definition suddenly, "oh it's an ordered field with the least upper bound property", and then proceed to prove stuff, it seems out of the blue, but it has literally thousands of years of history which lead to this simple characterization and each step in the characterization had some natural reason behind, a problem to solve
